page: Amazon Web Services r6in.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at a clock frequency of 3.5 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem consists of 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 vector extensions, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA instructions. The instance does not feature local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage via EBS alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark evaluations position the r6in.2xlarge consistently within median tiers for enterprise compute and memory workloads. The instance achieved 1891.99 on single-core stress-ng tests and 7709.54 on multi-core runs, alongside a Geekbench 6 multi-core score of 6017.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 11352.89. The memory subsystem demonstrates solid throughput, delivering 413.7 GB/s on small-block cached read operations and 56.36 GB/s on 256 MB uncached reads. In application-focused benchmarks, it reached 7.98 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 11.98 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

Performance tradeoffs emerge under compute-dense parallel tasks and large language model inference. While compression and basic cryptanalytic benchmarks align with average expectations, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 31.66 GB/s, ranking in the bottom quartile. Similarly, local 7B-parameter LLM inference was constrained by the 8 vCPU budget and CPU execution limitations, achieving 15.89 tokens per second in prompt processing and 7.03 tokens per second in token generation. The lack of onboard NVMe storage necessitates factoring EBS throughput and latency into overall I/O planning.

Resource allocation efficiency is dictated by the high memory density per core combined with elevated 12 Gbps baseline networking. The r6in.2xlarge is primarily suited for memory-intensive applications requiring stable network throughput, including in-memory caching systems such as Redis or Memcached, relational databases, medium-scale data analytics pipelines, and memory-constrained web application servers.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz. Configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores) and 64.0 GB of DDR4-3000 memory, it offers an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance provides 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without local instance storage, and includes no GPUs. In performance evaluations, the instance delivers steady mid-tier execution, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 11352.89, 7.98 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, and 56.36 GB/s uncached memory read bandwidth. Although constrained on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and LLM inference, its memory footprint and network capacity make it effective for in-memory caches, relational database workloads, and data processing tasks requiring significant RAM density.
